cues.en: whereas computer programs simply can't do it as well yet.

cues.en: For example, in the case of Ticket Master

cues.en: which is sort of the next evolution of captchas.

cues.en: So, let me tell you [how] this project started.

cues.en: So this project started from the following realization:

cues.zh: 事实表明，全世界的人每天
cues.en: it turns out that approximately 200 million captchas

cues.en: are typed every day by people around the world.

cues.en: But then I started feeling bad,

cues.en: see here is the thing: each time you type a captcha,

cues.zh: 基本上就浪费了十秒钟的时间。
cues.en: essentially, you waste ten seconds of your time.

cues.zh: 因为输入验证码要花十秒钟——
cues.en: Because it takes ten seconds to type a captcha --

cues.zh: 再乘以两亿人，全人类加起来
cues.en: and if you multiply that by 200 million you get that humanity as a whole

cues.zh: 每天大约浪费五十万个小时
cues.en: is wasting about 500 thousand hours every day

cues.zh: 在输入这些烦人的验证码上。（笑声）
cues.en: typing these annoying captchas. (Laughter)

cues.zh: 于是我開始觉得难受，
cues.en: So then I started feeling bad,

cues.zh: （笑声）
cues.en: (Laughter)

cues.zh: 我开始想：“当然，我们不能干脆
cues.en: and I started thinking, "Well, of course we can't just

cues.zh: 把验证码取消掉，因为网络的安全
cues.en: get rid of captchas, because the security of the Web

cues.zh: 多少依赖它们，但接着我又想，
cues.en: sort of depends on them, but then I started thinking,

cues.zh: “有没有办法把这份付出
cues.en: "Is there any way we can use this effort

cues.zh: 用在造福人类的事情上？”
cues.en: for something that is good for humanity?"

cues.zh: 事情是这样的，当你在输入验证码时，
cues.en: Here is the thing, while you're typing a captcha,

cues.zh: 在那十秒钟里，
cues.en: during those ten seconds,

cues.zh: 你的大脑正在做一件了不起的事。
cues.en: your brain is doing something amazing.

cues.zh: 它正在做计算机目前还做不到的事。
cues.en: It is doing something that computers cannot yet do.

cues.zh: 那么，我们能不能让你用这十秒钟做点有用的工作？
cues.en: So, can we get you to do useful work for those ten seconds?

cues.zh: 换句话说：
cues.en: Another way of putting it is:

cues.zh: 有没有什么计算机目前还解决不了的超级难题，
cues.en: Is there some humongous problem that we cannot get yet computers to solve,

cues.zh: 我们能把它拆解成一个个10秒的微小片段，
cues.en: that somehow we can split into tiny ten second chunks

cues.zh: 让大家每次输验证码时，
cues.en: such that each time somebody solves a captcha

cues.zh: 都能顺手解决这个难题的一小部分？
cues.en: they solve a little bit of this problem?

cues.zh: 答案是肯定的，而这正是我们目前在做的事。
cues.en: The answer is yes, and this is what we are doing now.

cues.zh: 你可能不知道的是，如今
cues.en: What you may not know is that nowadays,

cues.zh: 当你在输入验证码时，
cues.en: while you're typing a captcha

cues.zh: 不仅是在证明自己是人类，
cues.en: not only are you authenticating yourself as a human

cues.zh: 同时其实也是在帮我们数字化书籍。
cues.en: but in addition you are actually helping us to digitize books.

cues.zh: 我来解释一下它是怎么运作的。
cues.en: Let me explain how it works.

cues.zh: 现在有很多项目都在尝试将书籍数字化。
cues.en: A lot of projects are trying to digitize books.

cues.zh: Google 在做，Internet Archive 在做，
cues.en: Google has one, the Internet Archive has one,

cues.zh: Amazon 也正通过 Kindle 进行书籍数字化。
cues.en: Amazon, with the Kindle, is trying to digitize books.

cues.zh: 它的运作流程是这样的：首先你得有一本实体古书，
cues.en: The way is works is, you start with an old book, a physical thing,

cues.zh: 你们见过那种东西吧？就是……书本……
cues.en: you've seen those things right? Like a... book...

cues.zh: （笑声）
cues.en: (Laughter)

cues.zh: 首先，你得有一本书，然后去扫描它。
cues.en: So, you start with a book, and then you scan it.

cues.zh: 扫描一本书就像是在给书的每一页
cues.en: Scanning a book is like taking a digital photograph

cues.zh: 拍一张数码照片。
cues.en: of every page of the book.

cues.zh: 这样书的每一页就都变成了一张图片。
cues.en: It gives you an image for every page of the book.

cues.zh: 也就是每一页都对应一张包含文字的图片。
cues.en: This is an image with text for every page of the book.

cues.zh: 接下来的步骤，是让计算机能够
cues.en: The next step in the process is that the computer needs to be able

cues.zh: 识别出这些图片中的所有文字。
cues.en: to decipher all of the words in this image.

cues.zh: 这需要用到一项叫做 OCR 的技术，
cues.en: That is done using a tecnology called OCR,

cues.zh: 即光学字符识别，
cues.en: Optical Character Recognition,

cues.zh: 它可以抓取包含文本的图片，
cues.en: which takes a picture of text

cues.zh: 并尝试识别出其中的文本内容。
cues.en: and tries to figure out what text is in there.

cues.zh: 但问题在于，OCR 并不完美，
cues.en: Now, the problem is that OCR is not perfect,

cues.zh: 尤其是对于那些墨迹褪色、
cues.en: especially for older books, where the ink has faded,

cues.zh: 纸张泛黄的古旧书籍，
cues.en: and the pages have turned yellow,

cues.zh: OCR 无法识别出其中的很多字词。
cues.en: OCR cannot recognize a lot of the words.

cues.zh: 对于五十年前出版的内容，
cues.en: For things that were written more than fifty years ago,

cues.zh: 计算机大约有 30% 的单词都无法识别。
cues.en: the computer cannot recognize about thirty percent of the words.

cues.zh: 我们现在把计算机无法识别的所有单词
cues.en: We are now taking all of the words that the computer cannot recognize

cues.zh: 让人来替我们识别这些词，
cues.en: and we are getting people to read them for us,

cues.zh: 就在他们在网上输入验证码的时候。
cues.en: while they are typing a captcha on the Internet.

cues.zh: 所以下次你输入验证码时，
cues.en: So next time you type a captcha,

cues.zh: 你输入的那些词其实是
cues.en: these words that you're typing are actually words

cues.zh: 来自正在被数字化的书籍中的词，
cues.en: that are coming from books that are being digitized

cues.zh: 而计算机无法识别它们。
cues.en: that the computer could not recognize.

cues.zh: 如今我们用两个词而不是一个词的原因是，
cues.en: The reason we have two words nowadays instead of one,

cues.zh: 其中一个词
cues.en: is because one of the words

cues.zh: 是系统刚从书里提取出来的，
cues.en: is a word that the system just got out of a book,

cues.zh: 系统不知道它是什么，
cues.en: it didn't know what it was

cues.zh: 于是把它展示给你，
cues.en: and it's going to present it to you,

cues.zh: 但由于系统不知道它的答案，
cues.en: but since it doesn't know the answer for it,

cues.zh: 就无法为你评判对错，
cues.en: it cannot grade it for you,

cues.zh: 所以我们再给你一个词，
cues.en: so we give you another word,

cues.zh: 这个词的答案是系统知道的，
cues.en: one for which the system does know the answer,

cues.zh: 我们不会告诉你哪个是哪个，然后说：请把两个都输入。
cues.en: we don't tell you which one is which, and we say, please type both.

cues.zh: 如果你输入正确的词
cues.en: If you type the correct word

cues.zh: 对应系统已知的那个词，
cues.en: for the one which the system already knows,

cues.zh: 它就认为你是人类，
cues.en: it assumes you are a human,

cues.zh: 同时也对另一个词你输入正确有了一定信心。
cues.en: and it also gets some confidence that you typed the other word correctly.

cues.zh: 如果我们对十个不同的人重复这个过程，
cues.en: And if we repeat this process to ten different people,

cues.zh: 而他们都同意新词是什么，
cues.en: and all of them agree on what the new word is,

cues.zh: 那我们就又多了一个准确数字化的词。
cues.en: then we have one more word digitized accurately.

cues.zh: 系统就是这么运作的，
cues.en: This is how the system works,
